transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining the mediation-readiness huddle. As we all know, the former executive is demanding $425,000 to resolve the discrimination claim, and mediation is scheduled for next week. Our objective is to walk away with a signed settlement that includes a full release of employment-related claims and a final, clean separation of the parties. Before I approve any settlement terms, I'd like to go around the room. Let's start with our coverage counsel — what's your read on the claim's exposure and any settlement range you'd recommend? Then I'd like to hear from our client liaison on any business or reputational considerations we should factor in. After that, I'll make the final call on the resolution package.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I need to share an important coverage update before we go further. I reviewed the employment-practices liability policy endorsement and confirmed with the carrier this week that the authorized settlement amount for this matter is exactly $240,000 — that is the carrier's written authority. There are three conditions attached: payment requires a broad employment-claims release, there must be no admission of liability, and the carrier must provide consent before execution. I had not yet circulated the coverage confirmation to you, so I wanted to put this on the table now so it informs our mediation strategy. The demand of $425,000 exceeds the carrier's authorized amount by $185,000, and any settlement above $240,000 would likely fall outside coverage unless we negotiate additional authority from the carrier.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: During a call with the board chair this week, I confirmed that the company will resolve the dispute only if the agreement provides a neutral reference stating the executive's title and employment dates, includes mutual non-disparagement, and makes the resignation effective exactly June 30. This instruction has not yet been added to the mediation file, so I want to make sure everyone here has it before we finalize our strategy.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for bringing these critical updates to the table. Let me synthesize what we now have. Daniel, the carrier's written authority caps the settlement at $240,000, with three conditions: a broad employment-claims release, no admission of liability, and carrier consent before execution. That's a hard ceiling we need to work within unless we go back to the carrier for additional authority — and given that mediation is next week, I don't want to count on that. Marisol, the board chair's instructions add three non-negotiable terms from the company's side: a neutral reference identifying title and employment dates, mutual non-disparagement, and a resignation effective June 30. The good news is that the board's requirements and the carrier's conditions are largely compatible — a broad release and no admission of liability satisfy both sides. The challenge is the gap between the $425,000 demand and the $240,000 coverage authority. Here's what I'd like to do: at mediation, we open at or below $240,000, making clear we have authority to resolve within that figure on the condition that the executive agrees to the full release, neutral reference, mutual non-disparagement, and June 30 resignation date. We frame the $240,000 as a fair resolution that avoids the cost and uncertainty of litigation. If the mediator signals the executive will not come down to that range, we can request a recess and I will contact the carrier to seek additional authority — but only as a fallback. I am prepared to approve a settlement at or below $240,000 that meets all the conditions we've discussed today. Does either of you see any obstacles to that approach, or have additional information I should consider before I finalize our mediation authority?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I think the approach is sound and I don't see any obstacles from the business side. The board chair's three requirements — neutral reference, mutual non-disparagement, and June 30 resignation date — are straightforward and should be presented as standard separation terms rather than concessions, which should help keep the negotiation focused on the dollar figure. One thing I'd flag: since the board chair's instructions haven't yet been added to the mediation file, I'll make sure the written instructions are documented and circulated to everyone here immediately after this huddle so there's a clear record before we walk into the room. I'd also recommend we be prepared for the executive's counsel to push back on the neutral reference or try to negotiate the non-disparagement scope — those can become bargaining chips if we need to bridge a gap, but the board was clear that all three terms are required, so I'd treat them as non-negotiable unless you direct otherwise. From a reputational standpoint, resolving at $240,000 with a clean separation and mutual non-disparagement is a far better outcome for the company than prolonged litigation, regardless of the merits. I'm comfortable with the strategy as outlined.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Elena, I'm comfortable with the strategy as outlined. A few points from the coverage side. First, I'll circulate the carrier's written confirmation to you and the team right after this huddle so the $240,000 authority and its three conditions are documented in the mediation file alongside Marisol's board chair instructions. Second, I want to stress that the carrier consent condition is not a formality — it means we cannot execute a settlement agreement at mediation without the carrier's sign-off on the final terms. I'd recommend we build in time for carrier review during the mediation, or at minimum have a mechanism to get consent on short notice. Third, the broad employment-claims release required by the carrier should align with the company's objective of a full release, so there's no tension there — but we should make sure the release language is drafted broadly enough to satisfy the carrier's endorsement, not just the company's general release. If the executive's counsel pushes for carve-outs or narrower release language, that could jeopardize coverage. Finally, if we do need to seek additional authority from the carrier as a fallback, I'd recommend I be the one to make that request directly, since I have the existing relationship with the claims handler and can frame the ask in terms the carrier will respond to. I don't see any obstacles to approving settlement authority at or below $240,000 with the conditions we've discussed.
transcript.speaker: A2
